The '''Imperial Cultural Integration Decree of 1897''' was a Vesperan occupation policy applied to Belcanto after the [[Belcanto Campaign]]. Source material also calls it the '''Imperial Cultural Decree of 1897'''.

== Provisions ==

The decree promoted [[Vesperan Language|Vesperan]] in government, schools, and public institutions while restricting local cultural practices. It targeted traditional performance, local-language education, and public expressions of Belcantese identity.

== Effects ==

The decree was intended to integrate Belcanto into the imperial system. Instead, it helped make the [[Belcantese Language]], music, and historical memory into symbols of resistance.

Underground schools, private performances, coded correspondence, and preservation networks became central to the [[Belcantese Cultural Resistance]].

== Legacy ==

The decree became one of the clearest examples of Vesperan cultural policy in an occupied territory. Postwar Belcantese language restoration treated it as a symbol of what the new republic had to reverse.
